question:
A 87-year-old woman presents for management of type 2 diabetes. She has been controlling her
diabetes with dietary measures since diagnosis, and her glycated hemoglobin value has routinely been
below 7.0% until last week, when it was 7.4%. The patient has no other symptoms and feels well. She
has hypertension, which is well controlled with hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine. She also has
osteoporosis, which is treated with denosumab as well as calcium and vitamin D supplements. She
takes fluvastatin for hypercholesterolemia. Her blood pressure is 149/84 mm Hg, her weight is 58 kg,
and her BMI is 21.7. Laboratory findings are as follows: | | Patient value | Reference range | | --- | --- | ---
| | Creatinine (mg/dL) | 1.4 | 0.6–1.1 | | Estimated glomerular filtration rate (mL/min/1.73 m2) | 25 | ≥60 |
| Urea nitrogen (mg/dL) | 25 | 10–20 | | LDL cholesterol (mg/dL) | 94 | <130 | Which one of the following
next steps is best in managing this patient’s type 2 diabetes? Answer Choices: (A) Begin a
glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (B) Initiate sitagliptin (C) Continue dietary control alone (D)

Add a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor (E) Start thiazolidinedione therapy (F) Initiate basal
insulin combined with prandial insulin (G) Initiate metformin (H) Adjust dietary control and add low-dose
insulin (I) Initiate insulin therapy (J) Recommend short-acting sulfonylurea therapy
 A. Add a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor
B. Initiate insulin therapy
C. Initiate metformin
D. Initiate sitagliptin
E. Initiate basal insulin combined with prandial insulin
F. Recommend short-acting sulfonylurea therapy
G. Begin a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist
H. Continue dietary control alone
I. Start thiazolidinedione therapy
J. Adjust dietary control and add low-dose insulin
